text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Vietnam has demanded that China stop oil exploration which started 10 days ago 88 km (55 miles) from the nearest point of Vietnam's territorial sea base line and 103 km (64 miles) from the nearest point on the Vietnamese coastline, the Chan May Dong Cape. Although Vietnam's Ministry of Foreign Affairs immediately contacted China and Vietnamese maritime authorities made repeated warnings to the Chinese vessels involved, drilling operations were not halted.
-- Two children died and 28 people were sick after eating the meat of diseased cows in Phu Yen province.
-- Vietnam now has about 20 compact disc manufacturers, including 12 IT firms in Ho Chi Minh City. Nationwide demand currently stands at around two million compact discs a year.

-- Coffee export prices have risen this month to more than $1,400 a tonne from over $1,200. By March 10, Vietnam had exported 140,000 tonnes of coffee, an increase of 273 percent from the same period last year.
-- The State Bank of Vietnam plans to set up "life boat" credit to help commercial banks overcome risk.
-- In 1997 the Government will invest VND 108 billion, equivalent to 0.91 percent of total budget expenditure, for the development of science, technology and the environment.

-- Food companies under the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development purchased nearly 165,800 tonnes of rice in February, taking the total bought since the beginning of the year to 350,000 tonnes.
